primary_meaning: A prison or abyss of gloomy darkness into which God cast sinning angels, confining them until the final judgment (distinct from the final lake of fire).
primary_basis: 2 Peter 2:4 (the sole NT occurrence of tartaroō, describing angels cast into Tartarus and held in chains of darkness)
Jude 6 (parallel reference to angels kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until judgment)
Traditional Christian linkage to the fallen angels / Watchers tradition and the abyss as a temporary holding place for demonic beings

alternatives.meaning: Simply a synonym for hell (Hades or Gehenna) in general, without special reference to angelic imprisonment
basis: Broader popular Christian usage equating Tartarus with hell
Occasional older translations rendering tartaroō simply as 'cast down to hell'

alternatives.meaning: The lowest or deepest compartment of the underworld/hell, reserved for the worst offenders (drawing on Greek mythological layering of Tartarus below Hades)
basis: Classical Greek background of Tartarus as the deep pit beneath Hades
Some patristic and later Christian cosmological schemes of graded underworld regions

alternatives.meaning: A purely mythological or metaphorical allusion without implying a literal location or ongoing angelic confinement
basis: Critical/scholarly readings that treat the Petrine language as borrowed imagery rather than doctrinal topography
Emphasis on rhetorical purpose over ontology

notes: Christian interpretation overwhelmingly centers on 2 Peter 2:4’s unique verb tartaroō as denoting the confinement of rebellious angels; secondary associations with Hades/Gehenna or Greek myth exist but do not displace the primary angelic-prison reading in standard teaching and commentaries.
